title: 2. Can feedback-controlled finger gaiting qualify a scripted expert?
hypothesis: Feedback that alternates finger contacts while correcting pen-centre drift sustains axial rolling better than an open-loop finger oscillator.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the frozen open-loop oscillator from idea 1, rerun on fresh cases. A 0.20 sustained-success gain would justify contact feedback, but qualification additionally requires at least 0.90 success on each stage's 30 promotion cases.

protocol.command: gpu run bash -lc 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --research-protocol scripted_expert_qualification'
code_changes: Add lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/scripted_expert.py with bounded joint-target finger gaiting, long-axis angular-velocity feedback, and pen-centre correction using audited named observation fields rather than guessed offsets.
Extend the existing script/config with scripted_expert_qualification; depend on idea 1's tested adapter and episode reducer.
Freeze controller code and constants before opening these manifests; evaluate both controllers on cases 0-9 for screening and 10-39 for promotion in each stage, with no tuning on these cases.

Use the unchanged strictly positive paired t-interval rule for any promotion claim; tied success is not improvement. Separately report whether either scripted controller qualifies as a demonstration source.
Save full observation/action traces from qualifying episodes with manifest, controller, schema, and reducer hashes; document that these demonstrate axial roll, not end-over-end twirling.
Reference the briefing's completed negative pretrained-policy search; do not repeat it or silently substitute an Allegro end-over-end policy.

falsified_by: An upper paired interval bound below +0.20 rules out the predicted gain; failure to reach 0.90 sustained success means the controller does not qualify for that stage regardless of return.
direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This directly follows the user's scripted-expert-first instruction and separates absolute demonstration qualification from strict paired promotion. Its 240 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls are justified after R-038 establishes tested observation/action semantics and episode reduction. The weakest point is that interpreting controller failure before those interface checks would confound control quality with integration errors.

implementer.reasoning: Agree: the scripted controller must read named fields and be scored by the frozen reducer from R-038, otherwise a failure confounds control with integration. Re-triage as soon as R-038 is decided; it is the user's first-choice expert source.
